texts.facts: He was brought in a rickshaw to the hospital where he was declared dead. Learned Trial Court after hearing the parties vide order dated 30.03.2013 partly allowed the suit and directed defendant no.1 Rajkot Municipal Corporation to pay Rs.1,70,645/- to plaintiffs as compensation with 6% interest from the date of the suit till realization. Being aggrieved, the defendant no.1 preferred Regular Civil Appeal before the learned Appellate Court.
texts.arguments: It is thus the allegation leveled by plaintiffs that it is because of negligence of defendants firstly, in not controlling the stray animal at the place of incident and secondly, in not putting any sign board or cautioning activity at the site that the incident of accident and resultant death due to shock owing to instant fear and tension occurred. Plaintiffs have therefore alleged that defendants are liable to pay the compensation for the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined death of deceased for being negligent.

10. Issue no. 3 : Whether plaintiffs prove that the death of deceased Vrujlal was caused due to negligence and carelessness of defendants ?
It is the case of plaintiffs that deceased Vrujlal Popatlal Rathod was passing at the place of incident on the fateful day more particularly described in the plaint.
That the trenches 15 feet deep were dug for sewage and there were hillocks of soil dug on the two sides of such trenches.
That there is a vegetable market near to the place of incident.
That vegetable vendors too keep their stalls at the sides of the road at the site of incident.
That buffaloes suddenly rushed towards the deceased who had as result been caused sudden fear and tension resulting in to a heart attack.
That his Luna Moped fell in the trench dug there.
That in the hospital, deceased was declared as brought dead.
That the said fact has been affirmed by plaintiff in the deposition affidavit.
Plaintiffs have also produced panchanama of the site of incident at ex. 42.
In the said panchanama, it has been mentioned that there were trenches of sewage dug and there were hillocks off soil dug from these trenches of sewage.

It is true and acdepted by the parties hereof that the place of incident is near to the vegetable market.
That fruit and vegetable vendors throng the said place.
It is the Mochi Bazar area and a very busy place of Rajkot.
There is all probability that buffaloes were roaming around at the place to have free meal near the vegetable and fruit market.
The buffaloes suddenly running at the site in such a place of commotion does appear probable and possible.
As earlier held by this court hereinbefore that Municipal Corporation has a legal responsibility to control the stray animal like buffaloes.

This court can take even a judicial notice that stray animal roam around on the city roads and place of jaunt freely to the extend that one may force to think that such animal has the fundamental right to roam around and create obstacle in

Foreigners from the western countries take the photos of the stray animals sitting in the middle of road as souvenirs, as these sight is new and surprising for them.
But for the residents of our cities and towns, it is as common as cold.
Coming back to the place of incident, Defendants have accepted that trenches for sewage were dug and there were hillocks of soil dug from these trenches.
It was the morning time on Sunday, it can not be said that there were no fruit and vegetable vendors in and around the place of incident where there is a vegetable market just round the corner.
Neither it can be said that there were less number of people in the area of place of incident.
Defendants have not said in their depositions that precautionary signs or strings were attached at the place of incident to caution the people passing by that there is danger ahead.
In fact it was accepted by defendants that there was no sign board or string encircling the area of trench.

In fact there is no evidence NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/397/2023 ORDER DATED: 09/09/2024 undefined produced by defendants that any precautionary steps of putting sign board or string encircling the area of trench and hillock were taken.

In such a busy area, a person, nearing his retirement age confronted suddenly with few rushing buffaloes at a place where there are pits and trenches dug and there is commotion around, is at risk of his life.
Plaintiff side produced one judgment viz. 2013 AIR SCW 283 Mst. Param Pal Singh through father v. National Insurance Company.
In the said judgment, it has been held that stress and strain can cause heart attack.

In the scenario described at the time and place of incident, it can be said that a person of the age of deceased would have definitely undergone grave strain and stress on account of deceased finding no place to run away due to trenches dug
Even if deceased is taken as one suffering from heart disease, it can be said that his ailment is aggravated by the manner in and place at which incident occurred.
In the circumstances, it can be said without any doubt that defendants have remain negligent in their over all duty to do what was incumbent upon them to legally do.

It will have therefore to be inferred and held that defendants were negligent and careless and because of their carelessness and negligence death of deceased Vrujlal Popatlal Rathod was caused, hence issue no. 3 is answered in affirmative."
